primitives.name: Mask Fragility Index
primitives.verbatim_quote: 192 WALTER CAMP'S BOOK OF COLLEGE SPORTS man who intends playing behind the bat should wear a mask, and it is best to purchase a good one, as the cheap ones are likely to be fragile, not well made, and may perhaps be broken by a foul tip.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'F_m': 'fragility factor of mask material (dimensionless)', 'C_m': 'cost of mask ($) (dimensionless)', 'T_f': 'threshold force of foul tip (N)'}
primitives.assumptions: Linear relationship between material quality and fragility; cost scales inversely with durability.
primitives.breakdown_regime: F_m > T_f / C_m leads to failure during impact.

layer2.mapping: GSI Bayesian model for mask reliability; GSE dynamic risk adjustment for impact scenarios.
layer2.telemetry: Observed mask breakage frequency vs. cost category.

primitives.name: Body Protector Efficiency
primitives.verbatim_quote: A body protector is also an admirable invention, and saves many a bruise.
primitives.assumptions: Efficiency increases with material elasticity; rubber provides superior energy absorption.
primitives.breakdown_regime: E_p < F_i / (M_p * 10^3) results in inadequate protection.

layer2.mapping: GSI probabilistic injury prediction; GSE adaptive padding system.
layer2.telemetry: Bruise incidence rate per protector type.

primitives.name: Uniform Comfort Factor
primitives.verbatim_quote: A tennis or cricket suit, or any set of flannels, will answer nicely.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'C_u': 'comfort coefficient (dimensionless)', 'U_s': 'uniform style type (flannel=1, knickerbocker=2)', 'P_c': 'player comfort rating (0-10)'}
primitives.assumptions: Comfort increases with fabric breathability and fit; knickerbockers offer better mobility.
primitives.breakdown_regime: C_u < U_s * P_c / 100 leads to reduced performance.

layer2.mapping: GSI ergonomic design framework; GSE motion planning with uniform constraints.
layer2.telemetry: Player-reported comfort scores across uniform types.
